taste.name: Quiet surface, concentrated action
taste.trigger: When an agent interface needs many interactive states without feeling like a control panel
taste.decision: Chose a 95.5% white surface with #1A1A1A actions over persistent colored panels
taste.reason: People can follow the work itself while the next available action remains unmistakable

taste.name: Hairlines before containers
taste.trigger: When related controls need a boundary
taste.decision: Chose 0.5px rings and a three-layer low-opacity shadow over heavy borders or elevated cards
taste.reason: The boundary is discoverable at rest without competing with typed content

taste.name: Utility typography over display variety
taste.trigger: When labels, code, metadata and conversation text share one dense surface
taste.decision: Chose Inter at 11–16px plus Geist Mono for code over a decorative display/body pairing
taste.reason: Users scan changing states faster when letterforms stay stable across roles
evidence: 13px is the most frequent text size

taste.name: Motion explains state
taste.trigger: When menus, chips and enhancement states enter or leave
taste.decision: Chose 150–360ms state transitions with cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) over ambient decoration
taste.reason: Movement tells people what changed and where it went without adding persistent visual noise
